readiness_words: A data store this workload reaches changes protocol or has no assessed protocol, and its code migration decision is not answered: StackToIT keeps the workload blocked until the customer answers it in the decisions file.
validation_scope: A kubeconform check or a kubectl apply --dry-run of the manifest establishes YAML validity only, not behaviour: it accepts a REQUIRED_ token in a string field, an empty ConfigMap and a Secret that does not exist, and runs nothing; the checklist of the application compatibility contract and an application smoke test on the target are what show that the workload works.

containers.name: carts-service
containers.image_rebinding: pulled from where the source pulls it (Amazon ECR image public.ecr.aws/aws-containers/retail-store-sample-cart:1.6.3): decide where the images live on STACKIT, that the cluster can reach the registry, and the pull secret
probes: livenessProbe: exec curl -f http://localhost:8080/actuator/health (the ECS health check)
startupProbe: the same check over the start period

env.name: RETAIL_CART_PERSISTENCE_DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME
env.work: the value is not visible statically (a variable or an expression): set the key in the ConfigMap to the value the running service uses

env.name: RETAIL_CART_PERSISTENCE_PROVIDER
env.work: the literal value selects DynamoDB: the rewritten application selects the provider of its target data store instead (see the data store below); set the key in the ConfigMap to what that code reads (the value is not copied)

endpoints.source: carts:80 (the Service Connect alias of port carts-service in the namespace retailstore.local)
endpoints.target: carts:80 (the Kubernetes Service carts, port 80 → container port 8080, in the namespace the manifests are applied into)
endpoints.work: the Kubernetes Service keeps the name and port the clients call: check that they resolve it from their namespace; the Service Connect proxy (its retries, timeouts, TLS and metrics) is not carried

identity.target: open: the decision target.workload.identity (inputs.json) chooses federated_service_account (a Kubernetes ServiceAccount federated to the STACKIT service account of the role), service_account_key (a key of that service account mounted as a Secret) or no_workload_identity
identity.work: answer target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_ecs_service.this; until then the pods run with no identity and every call the application made with the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails
manual_steps: answer the input target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_ecs_service.this in inputs.json: with federated_service_account the draft writes the stackit_service_account of module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_iam_role.task_role, its federated identity provider for the SKE cluster's service-account issuer and the Kubernetes ServiceAccount carts in the manifest

until then, create a STACKIT service account named after the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_iam_role.task_role and grant it the role assignments the policies of module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_iam_role.task_role give (identity.tf lists them as the architect's variable)

federate it to the SKE cluster's service-account issuer for the subject system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:carts, and apply the ServiceAccount of applications/carts.templates.yaml (its annotation holds the service account's e-mail) in the namespace of the workload

change the application from the AWS SDK credential chain to the STACKIT SDK, which picks up the projected token: every call the application made with module.retail_app_ecs.module.carts_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails until it does

datastores.work: the application reads DynamoDB through its API and the target stackit_mongodbflex_instance.dynamodb_tables (MongoDB Flex) speaks another protocol: the data access code of the application is rewritten and a new image is built before the manifest is applied; a database engine swap is not an application migration

code_migration.question: The target stackit_mongodbflex_instance.dynamodb_tables speaks another protocol than DynamoDB: what is done about the data access code of carts?

options.title: the data access code of the application is rewritten to speak the protocol of the target store (the item DATASTORE_CODE_CHANGE is then done when the new image is built)
a target store that speaks the protocol of the source is wanted instead: the draft is regenerated with it, and the workload stays blocked until then

dns_dependencies.name: carts
dns_dependencies.source: a Service Connect alias in the Cloud Map private DNS namespace retailstore.local (module.retail_app_ecs.aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace.this): the clients of the namespace resolve it through the Service Connect proxy of their tasks
dns_dependencies.target: carts.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local (the Kubernetes Service carts; carts from a pod of the same namespace)
dns_dependencies.verification: resolve, from a pod of a client of carts, carts and carts.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local: expect the ClusterIP of the Kubernetes Service carts (kubectl get service carts)
